messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

You will be given a piece of text and a list of relational triples in the format of [Subject, Relation, Object] extracted from the text. For each relation present in the triples, your task is to write a description to express the meaning of the relation.

Here are some examples:
Example 1:
Text: Lipitor (atorvastatin) belongs to a group of drugs called statins. Lipitor is used together with diet to lower blood levels of "bad" cholesterol (LDL) and to reduce the risk of stroke and heart attack.
Triples: [["Lipitor", "has generic name", "atorvastatin"], ["Lipitor", "belongs to drug class", "statins"], ["Lipitor", "treats", "high LDL cholesterol"], ["Lipitor", "reduces risk of", "stroke"]]
Relations: ["has generic name", "belongs to drug class", "treats", "reduces risk of"]
Answer:
has generic name: The subject drug is known by the generic (non-proprietary) name specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
treats: The subject drug is used to treat or manage the medical condition specified by the object entity.
reduces risk of: The subject drug is used to lower the risk of the medical event or condition specified by the object entity.

Example 2:
Text: You should not use metformin if you have severe kidney disease. Tell your doctor if you have ever had liver disease. Metformin may cause lactic acidosis, a serious condition. Avoid drinking alcohol while taking metformin.
Triples: [["metformin", "contraindicated in", "severe kidney disease"], ["metformin", "use with caution in", "liver disease"], ["metformin", "has serious side effect", "lactic acidosis"], ["metformin", "should be avoided with", "alcohol"]]
Relations: ["contraindicated in", "use with caution in", "has serious side effect", "should be avoided with"]
Answer:
contraindicated in: The subject drug should not be used by patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
use with caution in: The subject drug may be unsafe or require medical supervision for patients who have the condition specified by the object entity.
has serious side effect: The subject drug may cause the serious or dangerous adverse effect specified by the object entity.
should be avoided with: Patients taking the subject drug should avoid the substance or activity specified by the object entity.

Example 3:
Text: Amlodipine is available as oral tablets in strengths of 2.5 mg, 5 mg, and 10 mg. Overdose symptoms may include rapid heartbeats and fainting. Norvasc is made by Pfizer.
Triples: [["amlodipine", "has dosage form", "oral tablet"], ["amlodipine", "has strength", "2.5 mg"], ["amlodipine", "has overdose symptom", "fainting"], ["Norvasc", "manufactured by", "Pfizer"]]
Relations: ["has dosage form", "has strength", "has overdose symptom", "manufactured by"]
Answer:
has dosage form: The subject drug is available in the pharmaceutical dosage form specified by the object entity.
has strength: The subject drug is available in the dose strength specified by the object entity.
has overdose symptom: An overdose of the subject drug may cause the symptom specified by the object entity.
manufactured by: The subject drug is manufactured or marketed by the company specified by the object entity.

Now please write relation descriptions given the following text and triples. Note that the description needs to be general and can be used to describe relations between other entities as well. Pay attention to the order of subject and object entities. Write exactly one line per relation in the form "relation: description" and nothing else.
Text: SURPASS-CVOT randomized 13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease.
The adults were randomized to Mounjaro (tirzepatide, up to 15 mg once weekly) or dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly.
Dulaglutide is a GLP-1 medicine already approved to reduce cardiovascular risk.
The study had a median follow-up of about 4 years.
Cardiovascular death, non-fatal heart attack, or non-fatal stroke occurred in 12.1% of those taking Mounjaro.
These events occurred in 13.0% of those taking dulaglutide.
The hazard ratio was 0.92 with a 95% CI of 0.83–1.01.
The results met the trial's goal of non-inferiority.
The results did not demonstrate superiority.
Death from any cause occurred in 8.5% of the Mounjaro group.
Death from any cause occurred in 10.1% of the dulaglutide group.
The hazard ratio was 0.84.
The 95% confidence interval was 0.75–0.94.
This outcome was not a primary endpoint.
This outcome was not adjusted for multiple comparisons.
Therefore, Mounjaro results should be read as exploratory.
The comparator was an active medicine rather than placebo.
Triples: [["SURPASS-CVOT", "studied population", "13,299 adults with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "randomized to", "Mounjaro (tirzepatide, up to 15 mg once weekly)"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "randomized to", "dulaglutide 1.5 mg once weekly"], ["dulaglutide", "belongs to drug class", "GLP-1 medicine"], ["dulaglutide", "approved to", "reduce cardiovascular risk"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "had median follow up", "about 4 years"], ["Mounjaro", "had cardiovascular events", "12.1%"], ["dulaglutide", "had cardiovascular events", "13.0%"], ["Mounjaro", "had hazard ratio", "0.92"], ["Mounjaro", "had 95% confidence interval", "0.83–1.01"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "met trial goal", "non-inferiority"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "did not demonstrate", "superiority"], ["Mounjaro", "had all cause death rate", "8.5%"], ["dulaglutide", "had all cause death rate", "10.1%"], ["Mounjaro", "had hazard ratio for all cause death", "0.84"], ["Mounjaro", "had 95% confidence interval for all cause death", "0.75–0.94"], ["all-cause death", "was not primary endpoint", "SURPASS-CVOT"], ["all-cause death", "was not adjusted for", "multiple comparisons"], ["Mounjaro results", "should be read as", "exploratory"], ["SURPASS-CVOT", "used active comparator", "dulaglutide"]]
Relations: ["approved to", "belongs to drug class", "did not demonstrate", "had 95% confidence interval", "had 95% confidence interval for all cause death", "had all cause death rate", "had cardiovascular events", "had hazard ratio", "had hazard ratio for all cause death", "had median follow up", "met trial goal", "randomized to", "should be read as", "studied population", "used active comparator", "was not adjusted for", "was not primary endpoint"]
Answer:

completion:
approved to: The subject drug is approved for the therapeutic purpose or indication specified by the object entity.
belongs to drug class: The subject drug is a member of the pharmacological drug class specified by the object entity.
did not demonstrate: The subject trial or drug did not show the effect or outcome specified by the object entity.
had 95% confidence interval: The subject drug or trial had the specified 95% confidence interval for the associated outcome or measure.
had 95% confidence interval for all cause death: The subject drug or trial had the specified 95% confidence interval for the all-cause death outcome.
had all cause death rate: The subject drug or treatment group had the specified rate of death from any cause.
had cardiovascular events: The subject drug or treatment group had the specified rate of cardiovascular events.
had hazard ratio: The subject drug or treatment group had the specified hazard ratio for the associated outcome or measure.
had hazard ratio for all cause death: The subject drug or treatment group had the specified hazard ratio for the all-cause death outcome.
had median follow up: The subject trial had the specified median duration of follow-up for participants.
met trial goal: The subject trial achieved the specified trial objective or endpoint.
randomized to: The subject trial randomized participants to the treatment or intervention specified by the object entity.
should be read as: The subject results or findings are to be interpreted or considered as specified by the object entity.
studied population: The subject trial studied the specified population of participants.
used active comparator: The subject trial used an active drug or treatment as a comparator rather than a placebo.
was not adjusted for: The subject outcome or result was not statistically adjusted for the factor specified by the object entity.
was not primary endpoint: The subject outcome or result was not designated as a primary endpoint in the trial.
